request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tx3 by TxPipe as an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Tx3 is presented as a framework that describes each protocol once with a verified interface definition and generates documentation, multi-language SDKs, and live JSON-RPC endpoints.
Through Catalyst Fund 14, TxPipe has put the developer layer into production with 5 protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, three per quarter, with developer and agent coverage plus development of an MCP server and skill framework.
The proposer claims there is currently no common interface mechanism across the Cardano ecosystem, increasing integration costs and limiting composability.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested amount is claimed not to breach the 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

Intersect states that funds will be administered through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multisig-style authorization rules, oversight entities, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 1,684,050 ADA for TxPipe's Tx3 open API and agent interface work, citing 12 protocol onboardings, MCP and skill infrastructure, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based treasury administration.
